title: Read the quarry as a process.
subtitle: Heat. React. Cool. Remove. Repeat.
summary: Explore Fóti’s proposed natron treatment: a heated surface reaction, removal of the cooled layer with a pounder, and a separate settling stage.
sceneDescription: A granite quarry surface with repeated scoops, an orange heated treatment patch, a dark pounding stone, and a cutaway settling vessel.
modelNote: A proposed cycle, not a chemical or thermal simulation. Color is explanatory; removal rate, temperatures, and pit dimensions are not inferred.

steps.name: Treat
steps.title: Apply material to the rock surface.
steps.text: Fóti proposes a natron-based treatment of granite. The highlighted patch identifies the proposed reaction zone; it is not a reconstructed ancient apparatus.

steps.name: Heat
steps.title: Sustain a surface reaction.
steps.text: In the proposal, strong heating enables a silicate-forming reaction. Achievable heat, fuel use, reaction depth, and residues are experimental questions.

steps.name: Cool
steps.title: Let the reaction layer cool.
steps.text: The colored layer becomes pale to represent a cooled product. This step matters: the proposal is not a pounder striking a pool of molten material.

steps.name: Remove
steps.title: Use the pounder on the altered layer.
steps.text: The dark stone breaks away the illustrated surface product. Turning treatment off shows the intact-surface comparison, without inventing a removal-rate advantage.

steps.name: Settle
steps.title: Separate a useful liquid fraction.
steps.text: The cutaway vessel illustrates Fóti’s proposed settling step. Identifying Aswan shafts as such vessels would need independent residue and context evidence.

issues.title: Repeated scoop-shaped depressions
issues.mechanism: Repeated treatment and removal of bounded patches could produce a family of depressions.
issues.remaining: Their form and residues must be compared with pounding, thermal damage, and other quarrying processes.

issues.title: Slow removal by pounding alone
issues.mechanism: A surface treatment could change what the pounder has to remove. It offers a specific comparison experiment.
issues.remaining: The Marčiš study measured mechanical pounding. Its results do not establish chemical treatment or supply its removal rate.

issues.title: Deep pits beside the work
issues.mechanism: Fóti interprets some shafts as settling spaces for a silicate-bearing liquid.
issues.remaining: The shape of a pit alone cannot establish its use; field context and residues are needed.

hypothesis: Fóti connects the proposed process with a reinterpretation of a workshop scene in Rekhmire’s tomb. The usual reading is metalworking; the image does not by itself identify a natron-on-granite process.
alternative: Mechanical quarrying with pounders, potentially alongside other treatments, remains the comparison. Experiments need matched stone and a complete accounting of heating and preparation time.
test: Compare untreated pounding, heating alone, and the proposed chemical treatment. Measure volume removed per total labor-hour, fuel, residues, and surface shape. Keep cooling and preparation time in the calculation.
